title: Refuse the forbidden ceiling key, fold the advisor case, warn on a dead chain key
action: Three config-layer fixes (role-edge-hardening D1 items 1-3). (a) validate_models_config in verbs/drivers/models.rs: a models.<rt> table carrying the key named by ESCALATION_WORD is refused by name with a FIX teaching bee cells escalate and citing decision 0015 - ceiling is an escalation flag, never a role, and a configured key currently makes prepare stamp marker ceiling PLUS a model param, the exact pair the guard denies (r3 A1). RED FIRST: a validation test with a ceiling key shown passing (accepted) on unfixed code via the current validator, then refused after. (b) verbs/drivers/guard.rs role_is_declarable: match the advisor arm case-insensitively (name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(ADVISOR_ROLE)), and in verbs/drivers/models.rs resolve_advisor: find the advisor key case-insensitively instead of t.get(advisor) - so a mis-cased Advisor key answers the SAME at the marker door and the --kind advisor door (r3 H1). Test: with Advisor:null both doors refuse; with Advisor:fable both doors resolve fable. (c) normalize_fallback_chains in models.rs: when a chain key is role-shaped (not provider/* and not a name that resolves as a concrete model selector in models.<rt>) and that role is not configured in models.<rt>, keep the chain but emit one stderr warn naming the key and why it can never fire (r3: chains are keyed on the RESOLVED role, so an unconfigured role-key is dead). Follow the existing junk-drop warn style in that function.

truths: A models table with a ceiling key is refused by name, teaching bee cells escalate; shown accepted-then-refused red-first
A mis-cased advisor key answers identically at the marker door and the kind-advisor door, in both the null and the configured direction
A role-keyed fallback chain naming an unconfigured role still publishes but warns once on stderr naming the dead key
No cell-role membership check is added anywhere - D7 untouched
